svg.title: Tire pressure, air, and temperature
svg.desc: Three pairs of before-and-after tires, each with a pressure gauge. (a) Adding air to a flat tire inflates it, but the gauge rises only from zero to slightly above zero. (b) Adding air to an inflated tire raises the pressure from half scale to three-quarters. (c) Raising the temperature of an inflated tire raises its pressure from three-quarters to nearly full scale. An animated companion below illustrates the process; its complete static alternative is shown for reduced motion and print.

g.text: Three ways to change a tire’s pressure
Flat tire: added air mostly fills out the volume
Fixed volume: more air means more pressure
Fixed volume and air: warmer means more pressure
Ideal gas, P ∝ NT/V. Gauge pressure stays near zero until the tire is full; then it rises with the
amount of air, and with absolute temperature.
Illustrative motion • slowed down • cycle restarts
